comparator.name: Tax Law
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted2026–2027 faculty OER B-4.2 and dated programme catalogue confirm a180EC compulsory Tax Law curriculum. This record contains30 positive-credit components totalling177EC. The remaining3EC Foundations of European Tax Law is compulsory, but the current course entry states a minor-enrolment condition without explaining regular bachelor access. The four Amsterdam Law Firm units in years one and two carry no separate EC; their skills assessment forms part of the semester project courses. No free elective space is invented from a generic website FAQ. The6EC thesis requires120EC registered in SIS three weeks before the semester, a fiscal-law topic and oral defence.
components: Taxation of Directors and Major Shareholders

A 6 EC individual scholarly thesis on a fiscal-law topic, presented and defended before two teachers. At least 120 EC must be registered in SIS three weeks before the semester starts; expected but unregistered results do not count.
Tax Law from an Economic Perspective

audience.programmeDescription: The University of Amsterdam’s Dutch-taught Tax Law bachelor combines legal foundations with taxation of individuals and businesses, tax procedure and legal research. Amsterdam Law Firm develops practical legal skills throughout the first two years as part of the semester project courses, without adding separate credits. Students complete an individual fiscal-law thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The table accounts for 177 EC of the 180 EC degree. A complete UCR comparison awaits confirmation of the entry condition for the remaining compulsory 3 EC European tax law course.

curriculum.limitation: This is a partial curriculum for 2026–2027. It shows 177 EC and leaves out the compulsory 3 EC Foundations of European Tax Law while its entry condition for regular bachelor students remains unresolved. The Amsterdam Law Firm skills units do not add separate EC.

componentNotes.y1-law-foundations: Introduces the scientific study of law, legal sources and ways to locate legal rules.
componentNotes.y1-criminal: Introduces criminal law and distinguishes substantive criminal liability from the procedures used to investigate and adjudicate it.
componentNotes.y1-private: Introduces legal relationships between individuals and businesses, including everyday transactions and contracts.
componentNotes.y1-state-admin: Studies the democratic rule of law, the branches of state power and their relationships with citizens.
componentNotes.y1-project-rule-law: A first-year project uses legal research and argument to examine constitutional change. Amsterdam Law Firm skills assessment is integrated into this semester project.
componentNotes.y1-intro-tax: Introduces taxation and its relationship to society, including taxes affecting individuals, consumption and businesses.
componentNotes.y1-intl-eu: Introduces international and European legal orders, with attention to the European Union and United Nations.
componentNotes.y1-prof-ethics: Examines legal professional codes and ethical conduct through realistic dilemmas and reasoned positions.
componentNotes.y1-family: Studies the legal position of individuals and families, including child-protection questions and the professionals involved.
componentNotes.y1-project-digital: A first-year project examines legal challenges around digital platforms, AI and public-sector algorithms. Amsterdam Law Firm skills assessment and the applicable Dutch language test form part of this semester course.
componentNotes.y2-tax-individuals: Studies taxation of citizens’ labour and investment income and the justification for distributing tax burdens.
componentNotes.y2-property: Studies the acquisition, protection and loss of rights over property, with applications to current legal questions.
componentNotes.y2-tax-dga: Studies the fiscal rules for a person who is both director and major shareholder, including the different treatment of wages and dividends.
componentNotes.y2-obligations: Examines agreements, contractual relationships and liability for harm.
componentNotes.y2-project-damage: A required second-year project connects legal knowledge and skills around damage and law. Amsterdam Law Firm skills assessment is integrated into the semester project.
componentNotes.y2-admin-law: Studies government decisions, the legal basis of administrative powers and their limits.
componentNotes.y2-substantive-criminal: Develops the principles that determine criminal liability, including attempt, preparation and participation.
componentNotes.y2-admin-procedure: Builds on public-law foundations to study administrative judicial protection, jurisdiction and the allocation of the burden of proof.
componentNotes.y2-formal-criminal: Studies the criminal process from an alleged offence through possible conviction and the procedural rules governing it.
componentNotes.y2-tax-procedure-project: A project applies tax procedure to a case from an assigned legal role, including taxpayers’ and inspectors’ rights and duties. Amsterdam Law Firm skills assessment is integrated into this semester project.
componentNotes.y3-european-law: Studies the EU legal order and the rights and duties it creates for states, individuals and businesses, including free movement.
componentNotes.y3-tax-entrepreneurs: Studies entrepreneurs’ taxation under Dutch income-tax and VAT legislation, including business forms and the concept of profit.
componentNotes.y3-legal-philosophy: Examines theories about what law is and how it should be, developing a critical position through philosophical argument.
componentNotes.y3-tax-corporate: Studies corporate income taxation of legal entities, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, alongside anti-abuse and societal questions.
componentNotes.y3-intl-tax: Studies international taxation, tax treaties preventing double taxation and measures addressing multinational tax avoidance.
componentNotes.y3-civil-procedure: Examines civil court proceedings, competing interests and the practical effects of judicial decisions.
componentNotes.y3-company-law: Studies business legal forms and their consequences for formation, representation and liability.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: A 6 EC individual scholarly thesis on a fiscal-law topic, presented and defended before two teachers. At least 120 EC must be registered in SIS three weeks before the semester starts; expected but unregistered results do not count.
componentNotes.y3-fundamental-rights: An integrating course examines fundamental-rights questions across the main fields of law.
componentNotes.y3-tax-econ-perspective: An integrating course examines interactions between tax legislation, business economics, private law and public law.
